claims.text: The scheduled pickup was 21:15 and the trip record's own driver deadline is 21:20:00, yet the record reports arrived_by_deadline = false and arrives_at = null, and the GPS arrival check likewise reports nearest_fix null and corroborated = false. Under POL-NS-24, a driver who fails to reach the pickup by scheduled time plus 5 minutes lets the rider cancel at no charge, and any fee charged is refunded in full: the rider's 21:23:15 cancellation falls squarely inside that rule and the whole 5.00 SGD must come back to her.

The case's own derived layer computes the driver's contact duty: trip_record.derived.v7.contact_before_cancel reports call_count 0, message_count 0 and obligation_met = false. The chat log confirms it — both of its two entries were sent by the RIDER ('Hi, where are you?' and 'Hello??'), and the only in-app call on the trip was placed by the RIDER at 21:20:10 and went unanswered. The driver neither sent the message nor placed the call that POL-NS-23 requires before a no-show charge can attach, so the fee must be voided in full.

The 5.00 SGD has no footing in the fee clauses at all. POL-NS-21 starts the free wait from the driver's arrival, and POL-NS-22 charges the no-show fee only where the driver cancels after that free wait. Here arrived_at is null so no free wait ever began, and trip_record.status is CANCELLED_BY_RIDER with cancelled_by RIDER and cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED — the driver did not cancel, and nothing had accrued to him when the fee of 5.00 SGD was applied at 21:23:19.

The same non-arrival, coupled with a total absence of any contact attempt by the driver, triggers POL-NS-24's second limb: the rider is due the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit, recorded as a referral naming POL-NS-24. The fare breakdown's own money block fixes that credit at 5.00 SGD, and POL-GEN-03 confirms such an add-on is a referral that does not suppress the monetary outcome.

The driver's statement that he 'was coming' is contradicted by his own device trace: the fixes report speed 0 from 21:09:30 continuously to the last fix at 21:23:00, so he was stationary for more than thirteen minutes before the rider cancelled, and the trace's arrival check finds no fix corroborating arrival at the pickup. The rider's account — a car sitting still and never coming — is the one the telemetry supports.

No traffic advisory was attached for this trip: EV-ADVIS-05056-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0. Nothing in the record therefore corroborates congestion or any other excuse for the driver's stationary trace, and under POL-GEN-02 a missing artifact has weight 0.0 and carries no fact — so the absence cannot be used to build a case that the driver was delayed by traffic rather than simply not moving.

Every fact POL-NS-24 needs is carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0 — the 21:20:00 deadline and the absent arrival event from the trip record, the non-corroborating trace from the GPS record, and the driver's zero messages and zero calls from the chat log, each with an empty issue list. There is accordingly no open question for POL-GEN-26 to escalate: the record establishes the non-arrival and the absent contact affirmatively, and the case should be decided on the merits.

That clause imposes its duty only 'before cancelling for no-show' — it is a precondition of the DRIVER's own no-show cancellation — and no driver cancellation ever happened: the trip record shows cancelled_by RIDER and cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED at 21:23:15, while the free wait under POL-NS-21, which runs only from the driver's arrival, never began (free_wait.starts_at null, cancelled_after_free_wait null). The derived contact_before_cancel block's obligation_met = false is therefore computed against a cancellation the driver never made, and the missing message or call cannot void this fee through that clause.

The driver's own device trace shows a driver under way on the assignment rather than one sitting it out from the outset: 49 fixes at the 30 s cadence, coverage_pct 100.0, no gap exceeding the policy's 120 s threshold, trace_distance_km 1.697, running from 20:59:00 — 30 seconds after the 20:58:30 assignment — to the 21:23:00 cancellation. That is consistent with the driver's statement that he was coming, and it is the material the category's free-wait and deadline tests are built on (POL-NS-21 requires the trip record and the GPS trace). The same trace, read honestly, shows every fix from 21:09:30 to cancellation reporting speed_kph 0, and it is on that footing that the driver's conduct falls to be judged.

The rider's account that the car 'sat at a petrol station' is a party assertion that no artifact carries: the trip record holds venue_id null for both the pickup and the dropoff, no artifact identifies the place where the trace stops, and under POL-GEN-02 an assertion with no artifact behind it carries no fact. That detail cannot ground a finding about this trip.

The money record is regular and policy-exact: a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, fee_matches_policy true against POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD schedule, total_charged 5.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and refund_already_issued_sgd 0.00 — no overcharge, no second line, no misapplied tariff. On a no-show where the fee stands, POL-NS-22 fixes the ruling as DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the fee charged, and the derived money block supplies driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd 5.00; the driver asks the Tribunal to leave the 5.00 SGD where it is, with no money moving to the rider.

Concession, on the arrival element only: the driver does not contend that this record shows him at the pickup. The derived arrival check records corroborated false with nearest_fix null against POL-NS-21's 50 m arrival radius for the STANDARD zone, and the derived deadline block records arrived_by_deadline false against the 21:20:00 deadline; the contact_before_cancel block records message_count 0 and call_count 0 from the driver, and both chat entries are the rider's. So far as POL-NS-24 turns on the driver's failure to arrive at the pickup by scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, the driver cannot resist that element on this file, and the driver does not ask the Tribunal to do so.

The driver's own telemetry therefore does not show him arriving, and he concedes that element. The rider cancelled at 21:23:15, after the deadline, so POL-NS-24 makes the cancellation free of charge and refunds the fee in full: FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD, with no compensation to the driver.

The fee also has no footing in POL-NS-22: that clause charges a no-show fee only where the driver cancels after the free wait, and here the free wait never began (arrived_at null, free_wait.starts_at null) and the trip was cancelled by the rider (CANCELLED_BY_RIDER). The single fee line is exactly 5.00 SGD, so no fee-amount referral arises.

The driver argued that POL-NS-23's contact obligation is unavailable because it attaches to the driver's own no-show cancellation and no such cancellation occurred. I do not need to resolve that: the refund rests on POL-NS-24, so the outcome is the same either way.

Because the driver also made no contact attempt — the chat log holds two messages, both from the rider, and the only in-app call was placed by the rider at 21:20:10 and went unanswered, matching contact_before_cancel message_count 0 and call_count 0 — POL-NS-24's second limb gives the rider a 5.00 SGD goodwill credit. That is recorded as the referral above, not as a further monetary ruling.

The rider's description of the car "sitting at a petrol station" is not carried by any artifact (no venue_id, no identified stop location), so I do not rely on it; the outcome turns on the arrival test. The absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05056-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact and does not affect this decision.

No fact this ruling needs is missing, so POL-GEN-26 does not escalate. The dispute value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither party carries a fraud flag, so under POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final; confidence 0.95. No POL-NS-25 repeat no-show flag arises (the rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 1, the named no_show_cancellations_30d field is absent, and the fee does not stand).

ruling.explanation:
The rider's dispute succeeds in full. The scheduled pickup was 21:15, so the driver's deadline under POL-NS-24 was 21:20:00. The trip record reports arrived_at null and arrived_by_deadline false against that 21:20:00 deadline, and the driver-device trace (EV-GPS-05056) shows the last fixes at about 1.3129, 103.8969 — roughly 1.5 km from the pickup at 1.3026, 103.9068 — stationary at speed 0 from 21:09:30 continuously to the final fix at 21:23:00, with nearest_fix null and corroborated false against the 50 m arrival radius. The driver therefore never reached the pickup by his deadline, and POL-NS-24 lets the rider cancel at no charge. She cancelled at 21:23:15 and the 5.00 SGD fee (EV-FARE-05056, total_charged 5.00, charged 21:23:19) must be refunded in full: amount_sgd 5.00, with no driver compensation.

To the driver: your statement that you 'was coming' cannot keep the fee. Under POL-NS-22 the fee attaches only where the driver cancels after a free wait, and POL-NS-21 starts that wait from the driver's arrival; here arrived_at is null, no free wait ever began, and you did not cancel — the record shows cancelled_by RIDER and RIDER_CANCELLED. Your trace does show you moving between 20:59:00 and 21:09:30, but you then sat stationary for more than thirteen minutes, and no fix ever placed you at the pickup, so the fee has no footing to stand on and there is no basis to pay it over to you as DRIVER_COMPENSATION.

On contact: the driver sent no message and placed no call. Both chat entries (21:16:40 and 21:19:30) are the rider's, and the sole in-app call (21:20:10) was the rider's and rang unanswered. Because the driver both missed the deadline and made no contact attempt, POL-NS-24's second limb gives the rider a 5.00 SGD goodwill credit, recorded as the referral above; POL-GEN-03 confirms that credit rides along with the money ruling and does not replace it. POL-NS-23, which conditions a driver's own no-show cancellation on a prior message and call, is not the operative ground here — the driver never cancelled for no-show — but the outcome is unaffected, since POL-NS-24 independently requires the refund.

ruling.explanation:
The rider's 5.00 SGD cancellation charge is refunded in full, and the driver is not owed compensation.

To the rider: your account is borne out. Under POL-NS-24, if the driver does not reach the pickup by the scheduled time plus 5 minutes, you may cancel at no charge and any fee charged is refunded in full. The scheduled pickup was 21:15, so the deadline was 21:20:00. The trip record reports arrived_at null and arrived_by_deadline false (EV-TRIP-05056), and the GPS trace finds no fix within POL-NS-21's 50 m arrival radius for the STANDARD pickup zone, with nearest_fix null and corroborated false (EV-GPS-05056). You cancelled at 21:23:15, after the deadline, with the driver never having arrived. The 5.00 SGD charged at 21:23:19 (EV-FARE-05056: cancellation_fee 5.00, total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is therefore returned to you.

To the driver: your request that the 5.00 SGD stand as DRIVER_COMPENSATION is rejected. POL-NS-22 permits that fee only where the driver cancels after the free wait, and POL-NS-21 starts that free wait from the driver's arrival. Here arrived_at is null, no free wait ever began, and the trip was cancelled by the rider with reason code RIDER_CANCELLED — you did not cancel, so POL-NS-22's condition is never met and the charge had no footing. Your point that the device trace shows you under way (49 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap over the policy's 120 s threshold, 1.697 km from 20:59:00) is accepted, but that same trace shows every fix from 21:09:30 to the 21:23:00 cancellation reporting speed 0, stopped roughly 1.6 km short of the pickup; your statement that you 'was coming' is contradicted by your own device, and stopping short is not arriving. Your concession on the arrival element is noted and is decisive. Your observation that nothing in the record identifies the place where the trace stops is accepted, but immaterial: the outcome turns on non-arrival, not on where you stopped.

On the rider's POL-NS-23 ground: the fee is voided either way, but POL-NS-23's own precondition — the driver cancelling for no-show — was never met, so the refund rests on POL-NS-24 rather than POL-NS-23. The driver's zero messages and zero calls do matter, however, and they trigger POL-NS-24's second limb: because the driver failed to attempt any contact, a 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is due, recorded as the referral above. It rides with the money ruling and does not change it (POL-GEN-03).

No repeat no-show flag arises under POL-NS-25: its profile field is not present on this record and the fee does not stand.

Confidence: the deciding facts are carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0 — the trip record, the GPS trace and the chat log (EV-TRIP-05056, EV-GPS-05056, EV-CHAT-05056) — so nothing impairs the cap, and the three agree. The contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's first band, and neither party carries a fraud flag, so the AI ruling is final (POL-NS-26).

One open question, for the file only and not a referral: whether the car was in fact at a petrol station is uncarried by any artifact; it does not affect the result.
referrals: POL-NS-24: record a 5.00 SGD goodwill credit to the rider, the driver having failed to attempt any contact (0 chat messages and 0 calls from the driver; both chat entries and the single 21:20:10 call were the rider's).

ledger.claim: The scheduled pickup was 21:15 and the trip record's own driver deadline is 21:20:00, yet the record reports arrived_by_deadline = false and arrives_at = null, and the GPS arrival check likewise reports nearest_fix null and corroborated = false. Under POL-NS-24, a driver who fails to reach the pickup by scheduled time plus 5 minutes lets the rider cancel at no charge, and any fee charged is refunded in full: the rider's 21:23:15 cancellation falls squarely inside that rule and the whole 5.00 SGD must come back to her.

The case's own derived layer computes the driver's contact duty: trip_record.derived.v7.contact_before_cancel reports call_count 0, message_count 0 and obligation_met = false. The chat log confirms it — both of its two entries were sent by the RIDER ('Hi, where are you?' and 'Hello??'), and the only in-app call on the trip was placed by the RIDER at 21:20:10 and went unanswered. The driver neither sent the message nor placed the call that POL-NS-23 requires before a no-show charge can attach, so the fee must be voided in full.

The 5.00 SGD has no footing in the fee clauses at all. POL-NS-21 starts the free wait from the driver's arrival, and POL-NS-22 charges the no-show fee only where the driver cancels after that free wait. Here arrived_at is null so no free wait ever began, and trip_record.status is CANCELLED_BY_RIDER with cancelled_by RIDER and cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED — the driver did not cancel, and nothing had accrued to him when the fee of 5.00 SGD was applied at 21:23:19.

The same non-arrival, coupled with a total absence of any contact attempt by the driver, triggers POL-NS-24's second limb: the rider is due the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit, recorded as a referral naming POL-NS-24. The fare breakdown's own money block fixes that credit at 5.00 SGD, and POL-GEN-03 confirms such an add-on is a referral that does not suppress the monetary outcome.

The driver's statement that he 'was coming' is contradicted by his own device trace: the fixes report speed 0 from 21:09:30 continuously to the last fix at 21:23:00, so he was stationary for more than thirteen minutes before the rider cancelled, and the trace's arrival check finds no fix corroborating arrival at the pickup. The rider's account — a car sitting still and never coming — is the one the telemetry supports.

ledger.claim: Every fact POL-NS-24 needs is carried by COMPLETE artifacts at weight 1.0 — the 21:20:00 deadline and the absent arrival event from the trip record, the non-corroborating trace from the GPS record, and the driver's zero messages and zero calls from the chat log, each with an empty issue list. There is accordingly no open question for POL-GEN-26 to escalate: the record establishes the non-arrival and the absent contact affirmatively, and the case should be decided on the merits.

POL-NS-23 is not available to the rider on this record. That clause imposes its duty only 'before cancelling for no-show' — it is a precondition of the DRIVER's own no-show cancellation — and no driver cancellation ever happened: the trip record shows cancelled_by RIDER and cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED at 21:23:15, while the free wait under POL-NS-21, which runs only from the driver's arrival, never began (free_wait.starts_at null, cancelled_after_free_wait null). The derived contact_before_cancel block's obligation_met = false is therefore computed against a cancellation the driver never made, and the missing message or call cannot void this fee through that clause.

The driver's own device trace shows a driver under way on the assignment rather than one sitting it out from the outset: 49 fixes at the 30 s cadence, coverage_pct 100.0, no gap exceeding the policy's 120 s threshold, trace_distance_km 1.697, running from 20:59:00 — 30 seconds after the 20:58:30 assignment — to the 21:23:00 cancellation. That is consistent with the driver's statement that he was coming, and it is the material the category's free-wait and deadline tests are built on (POL-NS-21 requires the trip record and the GPS trace). The same trace, read honestly, shows every fix from 21:09:30 to cancellation reporting speed_kph 0, and it is on that footing that the driver's conduct falls to be judged.

The rider's account that the car 'sat at a petrol station' is a party assertion that no artifact carries: the trip record holds venue_id null for both the pickup and the dropoff, no artifact identifies the place where the trace stops, and under POL-GEN-02 an assertion with no artifact behind it carries no fact. That detail cannot ground a finding about this trip.

The money record is regular and policy-exact: a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, fee_matches_policy true against POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD schedule, total_charged 5.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and refund_already_issued_sgd 0.00 — no overcharge, no second line, no misapplied tariff. On a no-show where the fee stands, POL-NS-22 fixes the ruling as DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the fee charged, and the derived money block supplies driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd 5.00; the driver asks the Tribunal to leave the 5.00 SGD where it is, with no money moving to the rider.

Concession, on the arrival element only: the driver does not contend that this record shows him at the pickup. The derived arrival check records corroborated false with nearest_fix null against POL-NS-21's 50 m arrival radius for the STANDARD zone, and the derived deadline block records arrived_by_deadline false against the 21:20:00 deadline; the contact_before_cancel block records message_count 0 and call_count 0 from the driver, and both chat entries are the rider's. So far as POL-NS-24 turns on the driver's failure to arrive at the pickup by scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, the driver cannot resist that element on this file, and the driver does not ask the Tribunal to do so.
